title: Counting bound in a real interval
statement: Fix $n \in \bbn$ and real numbers $a \le b$. Among the integers $j \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, the number of those satisfying $a \le j < b$ is at most $b - a + 1$.
hypotheses_covered: a and b real with a ≤ b
count over j in Fin n, i.e. j ∈ {0,…,n−1}
replaced:
For any $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and real numbers $a \le b$, the number of indices
$j \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ satisfying $a \le j < b$ is at most $b - a + 1$.
